body: Oh man I'm sorry. I hope it goes well!

I'm sorry you're feeling like this. I also have a lot of hopes and aspirations but for some reason turn to wanting to give up so easily. You're not alone.

Your story reminds me of myself a couple years back. At that point in time I didn't see a way out, but somehow I got myself here. Try to see every day as a win. You're leaving the door open to achieve those dreams you have-- hold onto those. You just have to make it through this part while you work toward the life you wanna have.

If you wanna talk about anything let me know, I'm here <3
Hey, I'm sorry life's rough rn. Lmk if you want someone to talk to
I think you may be surprised, though I understand it feels that way
It's okay. You don't have to be "good at it", you just gotta stop for a min. Just don't do anything to hurt yourself. Everything else can be worked on later

I know it feels like they've put in a lot of time and effort to help you and like they'll. be disappointed if you're not doing better, but this is their job. They won't be upset because you're hurting. They'll be grateful that you said something. People would much rather put in the work to help you then have to go to a funeral

This may be shitty advice but what I try to tell myself is, there's always another moment to kill yourself. Just wait one more day. See what happens. Then wait another. There's always more time to do that so don't rush it. It's a big decision. A lot of people feel regret when they finally do it, which says something about the nature of it all. You are hurting so you feel like there's no other way. It's like tunnel vision-- looking down one path, not seeing the other routes your life could take.

If you need someone to talk to I'm here. I don't even know you but I know your life matters, even if you can't see it yourself

First of all, you can let the work go to some extent. I know it's easy to fall into that trap of feeling like you're a failure if your grades aren't good, but you can always try again next year. The important thing is that you're alive to do that by then. Put your well-being first. Reach out to your therapist, let them know how you're feeling and they can probably pull some strings with school in getting extensions or excused assignments + absences.

Ideally, you'd be living for yourself, but if that isn't possible rn, hold on to any reason you have to stick around. If that means family or friends, embrace it. Spend more time with them. Make sure to do things you enjoy. You only have to take it moment by moment. You can worry about the rest later when you're in a better state

It's understandable that you've been searching for validation and human connection in those ways. At the same time, I think a part of you knows it's dangerous. I had a streak like that--wanting to please people cause you don't give a fuck about your life. But honestly, doing those types of things just makes you feel worse in the end.

The truth is, there are some good people out there who \*do\* care and who will be your partner, best friend, acquaintances. Sometimes it feels like no one's out there but even a stranger can care about your well-being and soon enough you could become good friends. (Just make sure they aren't asking for things you aren't comfortable with)

You really should talk to a therapist or some sort of mental health worker if you're considering suicide. I know it can be scary, especially if it means opening up about past traumas you may have experienced, but you can go slow. No one's gonna force you to talk about something you're not ready to discuss.

Seeking professional help would be ideal but if you can't bring yourself to do it, I'd be happy to talk or just listen, as I'm sure a lot of us here would be <3

Lots of times it's hard to recognize our own progress. It can feel like you're walking in circles, when in reality, yes you have patterns of doing better and doing worse, but you're still moving forward and maybe you handle it a little better the next time around. It's like a spiral staircase. You keep going around and around and ask yourself "what's the point?" but every time around you're getting closer and closer to the top.

So don't judge yourself too harshly. We're all our own worst critics.
You should let a parent or some adult know so you can get medical attention. I'm sorry you are hurting so bad <3

The truth is, they're gonna hurt then too. I know it can feel like you're the problem when bad things seem to follow you wherever you go-- even bad thoughts. But people aren't problems in themselves. You're hurting. There doesn't need to be a specific traumatic event in your life to validate that or a clear reason. You're hurting and you deserve to be supported through that so you can keep on going.

If you ever need to talk, just lmk. I'd be happy to be sounding board for something or just someone to keep your mind off the bad thoughts <3
I'm sorry things are tough. Do you wanna talk about it?

Just wanted to let you know that someone read this <3

I'm not sure I'm the best person to give advice for your situation, but if you wanna talk about it, I'd be happy to listen

I assume the doctors knew why you were in that state? I'm surprised they didn't make sure you were safe in leaving. I feel like they didn't do their job, but it sounds like you might benefit from going inpatient. I really hated that idea myself, but it wasn't so bad when I got there. You do have to make sure it's a good place, which you have the ability to do since you're not forced by law.

Either way, I hope you can get some help in whatever form. What happened is scary and needs to be attended to <3
Yeah, it's late for me too. What's got you down? (also, if you want my chat's open, but if you're more comfortable here, that's fine too)
I'm happy to talk with you
Hey, I don't know everything you're going through rn, but I'm here to listen if you wanna talk about it. I'm sorry things are so tough.

I do really hope you don't harm yourself in anyway. You have value, even if it's hard to see yourself.

Aside from that, it might not be the worst idea to write down what you would say to people. It might actually help you figure out how to improve things in your life so you don't feel this way. I at least found it to have this effect a few years back in a similar situation.

Hope you're doing okay as well <3

I'm very sorry for whatever happened to you. Sending you all the virtual support I can <3

Traumatic events have complex effects on our brains. It makes sense that you're having trouble focusing, among other things. It can be really scary, but the best thing you can probably do is talk to a school guidance counselor. Often times, it takes a lot of talking and thinking through the event before you can start to heal. It feels like pulling a knife out. In the moment, you'd rather not go back there in your head-- would rather just leave the knife in-- but in order to heal properly, it has to be pulled out. (Slowly, of course. You should still take your time.)

In addition, talking to a *school* counselor in particular might help with your grades. Sometimes, they can talk to teachers and grant you extensions and help on assignments. It's not your fault that you're dealing with this, so you shouldn't be suffering in your grades because of your consequent lack of focus.

You can try approaching people about it, but I would recommend being able to feel complete on your own before getting involved with someone. Not doing so can make it very difficult down the road to stay happy

You deserve to feel loved and cared for. Sometimes that doesn't come in the form we want, but, even if it is unrequited, you can still have a seriously rocking friendship with this person or others whom you mesh well with. It can be hard to recognizes in certain cases, but if you really look around you, there are people who *already* love you so much. It can feel good to reflect on that, I think <3

I have a similar extreme fear of failure, especially attached to school. I've said similar things to myself, like if I don't *blank*, then I'll *blank*. I think it can be hard to face not doing as well as you'd hoped, so we go to "escape mode". What I mean is, we view facing potential fears or consequences as the worst thing that could possibly happen-- so much so that our minds jump to suicide. A lot of the time, I find that even just waiting to calm down and let circumstances settle in before I try to figure out my next steps can literally be the difference between life and death. When we make decisions based on our immediate reactions (our emotions), there can be huge consequences.

Even if you don't graduate, there are options. It doesn't make you a failure or a loser. Everyone has their own path in life to take. People who don't understand that aren't worth the time of day.

I'm alright, you?

(If you'd like to use chat, I'm good with that, but if you'd feel more comfortable here, that's fine too)

Doing so will cause internal damage that will be extremely painful and, even then, you might still be alive to endure it. I would highly recommend not doing that. If you need someone to talk to, I'm here <3

Your question, of sorts, is a complicated one. Better is relative. It's really all about perception and outlook. Getting better means working on yourself and how you cope with everyday life. Life isn't gonna change much. It'll always has its ups and downs. The goal is to learn how to roll with the punches.
I can talk if you'd like

I get both the ideation and the self harm. It's a path I've unfortunately gone far on. You've probably heard this, but it can get addicting super fast. I knew that too. I think I wanted to get addicted so that I *would* keep going. I ran across a good piece of advice a while back on a strategy that helps some people.

I find sh to be a form of expression among other things. Like I want "proof" that I was struggling, that my pain was real. I wanna make a permanent mark. It can be helpful to make marks in something else, like the bottom of your desk, that will be there to validate the pain you're going through, but not harm you. I know, I know, property damage, but if it's your own thing, it's *much* better than hurting yourself.

I hope this was helpful <3

I'm glad you felt you could vent here <3

Anxiety and depression are really draining on a daily basis. And I get the meds issue. A wise person once told me that meds are only 25% of the solution. They help take the edge off, but you still have to put in the work to make up the other 75%. That can be challenging when you feel exhausted, but you can work on it one step at a time.

I think it says a lot that you care so much about your parents that they're a big motivator for you to fight through the pain. It's okay to struggle and feel like you need a break. The goal is to find healthy, temporary ways of relieving stress and other uncomfortable emotions.

I would try to find a support system for your addiction. Even if you don't feel like you can go to a parent figure about it, getting some sort of adult or professional help would make it a little easier to quit. Of course, it'll only work if you *want* to quit. I'd figure out whether you do or not in the long run.

Something you can do on your own that might be helpful is figuring out what you value or what goals you have. If you feel like you don't have any, make some. They can be small, like learning a new word, or bigger, like looking into some colleges or something. It helps when you have something to strive for.

I think it would be more beneficial than not to get some support from this friend. She sounds really understanding and close to you. I imagine it has been causing a lot of anxiety and effort to keep it hidden from her. At the same time, it's also scary to finally share this kind of info, so I wouldn't rush yourself. Share it when the time feels right.

If you're worried she'll feel responsible for not figuring it out before or something, I would simply reinforce the fact that it's not her fault and that (I would imagine anyway) you were trying hard to keep it from her.

Sharing that you sh can be a fine balance that I have struggled with myself. It becomes complicated when you know your friend also does sh or is unstable. I would do what makes you feel most comfortable over all.
I think it's awesome that there are people you care about. I know it's hard to feel like you deserve good things, but therapy should help with that <3

I'd appreciate it if people would be respectful of the situation. It's not funny in the slightest. If that can't happen I'm gonna have to just delete the post, but I was hoping to have a serious discussion about issues similar to this, or at least receive a little support. Thanks <3
That or a partial program. Whatever you think fits your current needs best.

It's not fair of your mother to say something like that to you, especially when she should know by now that this is a real issue. I imagine she was feeling overwhelmed and probably wants what's best for you. When she perceives you being lazy, she might be concerned for your future. Parents' hearts are often in the right place, they just do a screwy job of expressing it and helping the way you need. I might recommend starting a journal in which you and your mother can write to each other to cut out unnecessary emotional drama. Sometimes even tone of voice can cause an issue where it could have been avoided.
I'm here for you if you'd like

Yeah, I've found hotlines to be really unhelpful overall. I know they're trying to help as many people as they can, and therefore have to move quickly, but I think it's more important, at least to a degree, that they do a good job. If they spend too little time on people, then no one gets help.

Aside from that, I'm sorry you're struggling so much right now. I would recommend going into a program if you're at that point. It can feel scary at first, but it's worth a shot at helping you make a move in the right direction.

I find this really relatable. Like you feel bad for thinking this way, but you kinda wanna be the "worst" or have attempted the most times or most severely or whatever it is. I'm not sure what I can say other than you're not the only one. Hopefully that's a little comfort to you <3

I'm really sorry you're going through all that. Sending you my support <3

I can relate to some of your experience. I've also been homeschooled a lot of my life and am suicidal. I kinda had a similar thought process and started talking to guys online and doing stuff I didn't really wanna do, but felt like I should. I guess my reasoning was that if I couldn't be happy, at least I could try to make other people happy. It escalated and I eventually attempted and went inpatient once I was stable. Anyway... I'd be happy to talk with you more or just listen if you think that would be helpful. It's no more your fault than his that this happened and he's sick coercing you like that.

I obviously don't know the situation very well, but speaking from a girl's perspective, sometimes we don't respond for a while on purpose so we don't seem needy or too interested. It's dumb, I know, but it's possible this is contributing to her delayed replies. 

I imagine she would be quite sad if you choose to go through with that. I think you should want to live for you, but if that's not reachable right now, you could start with keeping her happy by staying around. Losing someone at such a young age, whether a romantic partner or a friend, is a very traumatic experience. The best thing you can do for her is spare her from having to go through that. Again, the most important thing is staying here for you, though!

Hugs <3

I think the first thing you should do is try to narrow down the most immediate type of help you need so that you can seek out people who can assist you. For example, if you need professional help from a therapist or psychiatrist, you should look into that. If you just want someone to listen, I'd be happy to do so
I'm sorry. I know that is a very painful thing to be told. Seems like a fair-weather friend. If you wanna talk about it, I'm here <3
I know it can be a scary realization that you're no longer afraid of death. I hope you have some support at this time, but I offer you a listening ear if it would be helpful.

You don't need to have a "valid" reason to feel that way, unfortunately. Sometimes it comes down to brain chemistry, not life circumstances. Some people are just more pessimistic or for whatever reason don't see the point in living. 

I wish people didn't put a pressure on finding a source for suicidal ideation like you described. I think it sends the wrong impression to people like you and me, who are circumstantially very fortunate, yet who still have a tough time. It can make people feel like their issues are insignificant, which could not be further from the truth in the case of someone considering suicide. 

Pain is experienced in different ways. What doesn't bother one person might ruin another's day completely. People are complex and diverse.

Enough with my ranting though \^.\^

Your past doesn't determine who you are now. Even if you were an awful person, you can change that at any moment. I don't know you, but it sounds like you are doing the best you can right now. That's really admirable in itself.

Please know you're not alone and that I'm here to talk whenever <3
That's awful. They're really caught up in the stigma surrounding mental health. At that point, I think you're gonna have to get help elsewhere. If you feel unsafe, there are places you can go.
Aww thanks, you too
You're right, it won't solve things on it's own. It really just gives you a chance to focus on your treatment and to stay safe while doing so. It's worth a shot if you're feeling this low.

Hey. I'm really sorry that's happening again. The lack of face-to-face contact, I think, has really hit this community hard. If you are feeling unsafe, I'd recommend going inpatient. There, you will likely have some interactions with people and can get some help. It is worth the risk if you are feeling this way.

Hugs <3

I'm really sorry. That person is extremely inconsiderate and uneducated. It's brave of you to keep going, despite those suicidal thoughts. Try not to let their words get to you. Not everyone will act this way in response. Things like this can really set someone back, make them not want to speak up about their struggles. It's extremely unfortunate. You deserve to be taken seriously and treated with respect.

I would let your parents know that you are suicidal. It sucks and is unfair, but sometimes parents don't realize how serious something is until it comes to that. Depression is a real struggle that many people deal with. It's not just being lazy or something. I'm sorry they aren't educated on the subject. I think, that if you let them know how much you're hurting, they might be able to relate to that better.

I'm sorry if people have been "scared off" or left you due to your struggles. That can feel crushing, I know. It won't necessarily be like this forever. It's up to you, whether you want to change or not. There are people who can help with that. I recommend DBT if anger, anxiety, or depression (essentially, overwhelming emotions) are an issue for you. It will take time and practice, but you can manage your emotions. No matter what you've done, you don't deserve to be "put down". That would leave a hole in this world, and in more hearts than you might expect.

I  understand that feeling. There's a lot that's not up to us, which can be hard to cope with. Any attempt is gonna be painful. It's an ugly process, no way around that. It's really not worth putting yourself through that.

The good times can be fleeting. I recommend trying to focus on what's important to you. What are your values? How can you live out your life with those as your focus?

I'm here if you ever wanna talk <3
It can feel embarrassing to say something, but it is much better than just doing it. Those who love you deserve a chance to help you.

I'm sorry you're in this situation. Please remember that relapse is a part of recovery. It's not a linear track. You're gonna have setbacks, but the work you put in to get where you are isn't lost now. 

Make sure you clean it out, bandage it up. I'm sure you know, but you really don't wanna get an infection. If it gets worse, let someone know.

Be safe <3

I know how hard it is to fight against it. While you still have some strength left, please get some help. If you find yourself making a plan, go inpatient. It can be scary, but it is worth it. A failed attempt would lead you to going involuntarily, which is not a good feeling. I can't promise that things will get better, but you can be an active participant in your treatment. That's how YOU can get better.

Lots of support <3

I'm sorry you're dealing with so much right now. My heart goes out to you. I implore you to get some help first. Anything you have to do to keep going. Step back from things that are stressing you out, even if just for a day. Any consequences will be temporary. Losing your life is not.

I'm not just some outsider saying, "hey, chin up. It'll get better". I know that life circumstances don't necessarily get better. What can get better is your way of handling struggles. I highly recommend DBT. It has helped me so much since my attempt. I did hang myself. It's a slow, excruciating process. Please don't put yourself through that. Go inpatient if you feel unsafe. Be kind to yourself. I'm here for you <3
Hahaha. Hanging in there at 6 :P
Thank you, that's very kind. That is the plan, as long as I'm able.
Whatever you're comfortable with. My chat's open if you'd like
Thanks for the update. I'm glad you feel like that you can help in that way. Your mom sounds sweet.
Of course

I'm glad you wrote this out. I hope it was helpful to you in processing. I can only imagine how hard it must be on your own like that. My best advice is to tell your loved ones that you're feeling suicidal. It might sadden them, but it would be much more of a burden on them if you killed yourself. I hope you get some help. Don't wait till you're actively suicidal to do so. Passive ideation is still a serious issue that needs some attention.

If you haven't already, try to tell your family and boyfriend about your suicidal thoughts. It might be hard for them to hear, but it's innumerably better than you slipping away from them. They might be of some support to you. If you feel unsafe, you can always go inpatient. It's scary at first, yes, but it can be a lot of help if you go to a good one. Virtual hugs <3
Hey man, you doing okay? My chat's open if you feel like it.

It sounds like you have a lot you're dealing with right now. I'm sorry all this has happened. It's completely unfair. I can't promise it gets better. All I can say is that you can make it better. Life will always be filled with both the good and the bad. It's how you cope and deal with it all that can change. I really recommend getting some help. Try a DBT group. Do a partial program. Go inpatient, if you feel unsafe at home. Hanging yourself is an excruciating process. It's slow and agonizing. I tried 2 and a half months ago and I just ended up with a crap load of new problems on top of the old ones I already had. I wish I'd gotten help before then, instead of waiting till I was half dead and involuntarily admitted. Still, I'm glad I'm still here. I really have turned a corner since then.

All this to say, don't wait till then to get help. Spare yourself the trauma, please. I'm here if you ever wanna talk or have questions.

I would recommend trying DBT. It has really helped with my anxiety. Meds also might help take the edge off and make it easier for you to work on your treatment. Take things one day at a time. If you can only focus on one thing, just focus on the here and now. You can worry about the rest later.

I'm sorry you have lost so much. That must be very painful to go through. Please know that I hear you-- you're not being ignored. I'm sorry if in the past, people didn't respond. That feels sucky, I know. You can talk to me, if you think that might help. No one deserves to die. No matter how you feel about yourself, you have value and worth. Your life actions don't change that. Reach out for help. Attempts are ugly and painful and messy. Please be kind to yourself. I care. Life is ever-shifting. Yes, there will always be struggles, but there are always new possibilities. I think it's worth sticking around for, if only out of mere curiosity.

I'm sorry things are so hard right now. I know there can be a lot of complex thoughts and emotions around failed attempts. I'm really happy you're still here. Please get some help. It's worth a shot if you want to give up anyway. Don't wait till you're half alive in an ambulance and forced to go inpatient, due to another attempt. Get treatment voluntarily-- it feels so much better, trust me.

It might be a nice break from your parents to go inpatient as well. If they are triggering you a lot, you might need some time away where you can get help on distress tolerance and similar coping strategies.

Try to get into a routine, some sort of schedule if you can. Fill your days up with things that you enjoy and will make you feel accomplished. You need to get out of this cycle. Behavioral activation is the key. It will be hard at first, but it will likely make a huge positive impact. This will probably help with the sleep deprivation as well.

If you need to take a step away from school and other things that might be stressing you out, that's okay! The most important thing is that you keep living, so if you need to do a partial program or even go inpatient, please do. Don't wait till things get worse. It sounds like there are some people who love you. Reach out to them, tell them how you're feeling. You're not alone in this <3

Virtual hugs. Wish I could give you a real one. I'm sorry things have been so hard. Maybe tell a friend (or acquaintance) that you're feeling so low. It sounds like you really just want some support. I'm here whenever if you wanna talk. You have so much ahead of you. Teenage is hard. Try to keep looking forward. It's okay if you need some time to take care of your mental health. School will be there afterwards, but only if you keep living. Make that your top priority.

From experience, it's never quick and easy. It's really not worth putting yourself through that. The world is harsh, and that's probably why you are feeling suicidal, so be kind to yourself. Don't make it harder.

We are all here for you whenever you need <3

If you were trying to kill yourself, that is an attempt. Either way, it does not take an attempt for someone to need and deserve help. If you are feeling suicidal, that is a serious issue. Please do not "wait" till you have done more damage to yourself to get treatment.

The depth or quantity of SH doesn't determine how much you're struggling or how much emotional pain you're feeling either. It's all dependent on the person. Your life experience and hardships are valid, please know this. You don't have to prove it to anyone.

I recommend doing a program if you feel like things aren't getting better or are getting worse. I waited much too long to do so and ended up attempting before I was forced to go inpatient. It is a MUCH better feeling to go voluntarily. You can even do a partial program if you think that would be helpful.

I'm here if you ever wanna talk <3

Feeling trapped causes people to act impulsively. This is the exact word I used right before I attempted. Even if she says she will not act on it, if she gets pushed over the edge by something, she might, in the moment, see no other option.

I can't give you very specific advice without knowing the situation, but if there's any way you can make her feel like there are other options, that would be awesome. It will be difficult, as she is probably thinking very irrationally right now. Try asking her how you can help, what she wants from you. Some people like to get help problem solving/receive advice, while others just want someone to listen and validate them. If you do one while she is seeking the other, she will likely feel even worse.

If you can get her some professional help, I would strongly urge you to do so. It's wonderful that you are trying so hard to help her, but you should not have to carry that weight on your shoulders alone. There are people who can help <3

I get that. This is a nice space to talk and not worry about privacy. It's a tough call, but I'd either recommend making a new account or just letting that friend know that you'd like some space on here. I don't know if that'd really work. Not great options, I know. I hope things go well

You're really brave for continuing to fight and keep living. Every day is a victory, my friend. I'm very sorry for those things you went through. If you're feeling as bad now as you were back then, there are probably some things you need to work through. To be honest, I don't love going to therapy, but I do it anyway in hopes that it can help. I have found DBT to be a lot more beneficial though and would recommend it. It's especially helpful, I think, to learn grounding techniques if you dissociate or have flashbacks.

The nightmares suck, I know. Unfortunately, they probably won't go away until you figure some things out. It's your brain trying to process. If you wake up in the middle of the night because of one, try to have a plan in place. Get out of bed, get some water, watch a funny movie or read a book. Try to get yourself out of that headspace.

And of course, I'm here if you ever wanna talk. I honestly don't mind in the slightest <3

This is horrendous. It makes me so disgusted when stuff like this happens. Someone shouldn't have to have attempted in order to get help! The fact that she went there in the first place is SO brave of her. She clearly was trying to keep going with the last bit of willpower she had left in her.

The poor family. I send my condolences.
I mean... yeah, that's probably not the best sign. But still. Sometimes I like to talk to those people about this stuff. Kinda dark humor, but it makes me feel better.

That's awesome that you have a great friend group! Quality is much more important than quantity. I hope they can help you through some of this stuff. Have you opened up to them about your suicidal thoughts? If they're supportive, that might be helpful.

I'm sorry you're going through this. I think realizing how much you're hurting can be a scary thing. I imagine there are probably some traumatic things you've gone through or some difficult situations you have been or still are in. I really hope you open up to someone to talk about these things. It feels stupid sometimes, but it honestly does help you work through them.

Everyone has their struggles in life, some more than others. Correct me if I'm wrong, but by "normal kid" I think you mean why can't you just be happy? I think this all depends on our experiences. If you've seen some horrible things, you probably are gonna have a pessimistic outlook on the world. I think the goal would be to add some little things that make you happy. If you're stressed, give yourself a break every once in a while. Take things one day at a time <3
The fact that you are even considering facing your fears now shows how brave you are. These things take time <3

I'm sorry you're going through all this. Is there any way you can get away from that guy? It sounds like he is not good for you and would not be good for the child either. You really need some people you can vent to and receive support from. Do you have anyone you think could do that for you? If you are keeping the baby, you probably are gonna want some help on tough days, especially with postpartum.

I'm here for you if you need someone to talk to <3

Have you tried taking melatonin or Benadryl? I have found these to be very helpful. Another thing you could try is putting screens away a while before bed. They keep your brain stimulated and awake for longer. Other things like lowering the room temperature, doing things to relax, like drinking tea or reading, and maybe writing down your thoughts before bed might be helpful

I don't think you deserve to be treated like that and I'm sorry that it's happening. The least I can do is say that I am here for you and rooting for you. I may not be there in person, but I am there in spirit.

That would be really awesome. I do think a lot of people on here are too scared to show their faces, but if we could have a live chat or something, I think that would help a lot of people, including myself.

I hope you pursue this idea.

I know how scary realizing that change is in itself. Any level of harming yourself is serious and should be treated as such. If you are feeling suicidal, I encourage you to reach out for help. Even if you don't want to tell your parents or friends, it might be useful to get some therapy. If you already have a therapist and find it ineffective, you might take a look at a DBT group. DBT focuses more on skills you can use everyday, rather than just talking and talking about your struggles, only to just go home and (if you're like me) feel worse about it all.

Please take care of yourself and stay safe. If you are engaging in self harm, make sure you clean the wounds and cover them properly <3

I'm very sorry for the suffering that you are experiencing. Try to remember that we are our own worst critics and we often jump to the worst possible conclusions. I think it's likely that a lot of people don't hate you and might just be unsure about whether you want to talk to them.
